timing: Prospective third dataset, added after the two trajectory validation choices and before inspecting either of their test results. Report it separately from those two registered primary comparisons.
hypothesis: Four copies of each gas-sensor model measure the same exposure. If copies are exchangeable for discrimination after normalization, equal weights for the same feature on those sensors remove nuisance variation. Known hardware groups provide an independent reference, but drift or calibration can make unequal weights optimal. An advantage over a permutation alone does not establish an advantage over full Dense or hardware grouping.
source: Gas Sensor Array Drift at Different Concentrations, UCI 270. Use the first five gas labels present in every period; toluene is absent from three early source periods. Each complete measurement is one observation, use only the 128 sensor responses. Concentration and time are not predictive inputs. Apply signed log1p then standardize each feature using only source-fitting records, clip to [-8,8] for all stages.
split: Time batches 1-5 supply five source tasks, one task per period, 75 percent stratified training per class in each period and the remainder for numerical validation. Batches 6 and 7 each supply 256 independent 2-shot validation episodes. Freeze choices before prediction on batches 8,9,10. Each test period supplies 512 independent balanced 5-way episodes with the same 12 query readings per gas at 2- and 5-shot. No reading repeats inside an episode. Numerical starts independent across batches of 32 paired episodes.
fit: Use the same Dense source and target optimizer as in the trajectory study, 32 ReLU hidden neurons, three independent source starts, 800 source steps, 1200 for the pooled source Dense. Refit numerical target weights at 0.01 Adam, independently choose 25/75/200 updates on validation (also zero for pooled pretrained). Paired fixed-index versus from-scratch Dense; also evaluate a narrower Dense with the same first-layer parameter count and four common row permutations of the selected indexator.
selection: Offer both manuscript Algorithm 1 Ward families at all four budgets. Fix the greatest mean validation accuracy averaged equally over the two periods, then least half-Brier, smaller budget, fewer updates, lexical name. Additionally freeze the best of the same two families at 1024 codes, the natural hardware budget; compare it to the known physical map and four permutations of this physical-budget aSRR at equal cost.
hardware: Channel order is 2602,2602,2600,2600,2610,2610,2620,2620 repeated twice as documented by the dataset authors. Tie only the same one of eight features across the four duplicate sensors of each type, separately per neuron, giving 32 independent weights per neuron and 1024 total. Report precision and recall of all signed pair ties of the physical-budget learned map relative to these hardware equalities and its permutations. Hardware groups are a physical reference, not guaranteed optimal classifier weights.
inference: Primary contrast for this extension is 2-shot validation-selected Algorithm 1 minus tuned Dense, equal weight per test time period. Report all three periods, the combined difference and descriptive stratified 95 percent Monte Carlo interval conditional on these three batches. Additionally show simultaneous 98.33 percent intervals across all three datasets as a conservative three-dataset summary. Five-shot and fixed hardware-budget contrasts are secondary, use 95 percent intervals. A point gain >=1 pp with a simultaneous lower bound above zero is considered noticeable.
